name: Leo Minor
introduction: is the Little Lion, a faint group of stars between Leo and the Great Bear, introduced by Johannes Hevelius in 1687. It is best seen on dark northern spring evenings.

sections.title: What makes it special
paragraphs: Leo Minor has no Alpha star: when Francis Baily assigned Greek letters in 1845, he gave only Beta to a star here. Its brightest star, [Praecipua](hip:53229), therefore has no Greek letter at all.

sections.title: Notable stars
paragraphs: [Praecipua](hip:53229) is an orange giant about 100 light-years away. [Beta Leonis Minoris](hip:51233) is a binary of two giant stars.

sections.title: Beyond the stars
paragraphs: In 2007, Dutch schoolteacher Hanny van Arkel, a volunteer in the Galaxy Zoo project, discovered a strange green glowing cloud near the galaxy IC 2497 in Leo Minor. The cloud, now known as Hanny’s Voorwerp, is lit by light from the galaxy’s once-active black hole.
